title: Graceful Degradation
summary: Preserve the most valuable safe subset of service during dependency failure, making reduced capability and evidence freshness explicit to users.
overview: Graceful degradation deliberately reduces functionality when full service cannot be delivered. An agent might provide verified cached information, omit an optional enrichment, queue a long task, or return a structured partial result. The degraded mode must have its own correctness contract rather than merely returning whatever content happens to be available.

Classify dependencies and capabilities by business consequence. Losing a recommendation model may permit a search-only experience; losing authorization cannot justify unrestricted access. Define which facts may be stale, which actions are disabled, and how the interface communicates limitations without falsely claiming complete success.

production.poc: A prototype can disable one dependency at a time and identify which useful functions remain. Write down the minimum acceptable response for each failure.
production.production: Production implements explicit capability states, fallback ordering, freshness limits, and observability for degraded responses. Keep degraded modes exercised so they do not become untested emergency code.
production.scale: At scale, avoid shifting all traffic onto an undersized fallback. Capacity reservations, admission control, and recovery hysteresis prevent degradation from triggering another outage.

components.name: Capability map
components.role: Relates user-visible functions to mandatory and optional dependencies.

components.name: Health and policy evaluator
components.role: Determines which degraded modes are currently safe and permitted.

components.name: Fallback provider
components.role: Supplies validated cached data, simpler computation, alternative models, or queued work.

components.name: Response contract
components.role: Marks missing capabilities, evidence freshness, and incomplete outcomes explicitly.

components.name: Recovery controller
components.role: Restores normal service gradually and observes fallback capacity and errors.

flow.title: Assess dependency state
flow.description: Detect timeout, open circuit, unavailable data, or exhausted capacity using trusted signals.

flow.title: Select permitted mode
flow.description: Consult the capability map and preserve mandatory security and correctness constraints.

flow.title: Bound fallback demand
flow.description: Apply admission and concurrency limits before moving work to alternate capacity.

flow.title: Produce useful subset
flow.description: Return only results that meet the degraded contract and freshness requirements.

flow.title: Explain limitations
flow.description: Identify missing analysis or disabled actions without presenting partial service as complete.

flow.title: Recover gradually
flow.description: Probe primary health and restore capabilities with hysteresis and outcome monitoring.

useCase.title: Keeping store support useful during model outage
useCase.situation: A retailer's store assistant answers operating-procedure questions and explains current stock exceptions.
useCase.problem: When the language-model provider is unavailable, the entire support interface becomes unusable even though approved procedures remain searchable.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must preserve access to verified information while disabling unsupported analysis and stock-changing actions.
useCase.architecture: A capability map selects search-only mode for procedure questions and queues analytical requests that require unavailable inference.
runtime: A store manager asks for a returns procedure; the interface shows relevant approved source passages with their version dates.
A complex stock question receives a deferred-operation identifier and a clear description of the unavailable analysis.
useCase.failure: If cached inventory exceeds its freshness limit, the system withholds availability claims rather than showing stale stock as current.
useCase.impact: Track successful degraded tasks, fallback saturation, stale-data rejection, and time to restore full capability. Availability is measured against each mode's promised behavior.

tradeoffs.benefit: Users can complete some work during an outage.
tradeoffs.cost: Additional modes increase implementation and testing effort.

tradeoffs.benefit: Responses remain fast when origins fail.
tradeoffs.cost: Freshness limits restrict which claims remain valid.

tradeoffs.benefit: Important tasks can survive temporary capacity loss.
tradeoffs.cost: Users need durable status and realistic completion expectations.

failures.scenario: Fallback capacity overloads after primary failure
failures.detection: Queue age and rejection rate rise sharply in the alternate path.
failures.recovery: Shed optional work and enforce reserved capacity limits.

failures.scenario: The interface labels a partial result complete
failures.detection: Contract checks find missing mandatory sections without status markers.
failures.recovery: Correct the response state and block misleading publication.

mistakes.fix: Enforce freshness bounds and show source age.
Exercise them in routine validation and controlled failure tests.

whenToUse: Useful safe capabilities survive some dependency failures.
Users can understand and act on partial results.
Fallback capacity and freshness can be bounded.
whenNotToUse: A partial result would be misleading or unsafe.
Mandatory authorization or integrity controls are unavailable.
The fallback has no validated correctness contract.
checklist: Expose partial and deferred status clearly.
Test gradual restoration and mode switching.
